purpose: Build a small Android APK inside Quest Termux, install it through an already authorized WiFi ADB endpoint, and launch it into a visible Quest panel.
authority_boundary: Termux owns the source checkout and local build output only.
ADB shell authority comes from an operator-approved debugging session.
The recipe does not pair, bypass authorization, become HOME, or install a hidden boot watchdog.
Generated APKs, idsig files, debug keystores, platform jars, screenshots, logs, and real package names stay out of the repository.

preflight.label: workflow
preflight.command: Activate the team's Meta Quest workflow for live device coordination.

preflight.label: adb-authority
preflight.command: Enable or pair WiFi ADB through an already authorized external route.

preflight.label: termux-tools
preflight.command: pkg install android-tools openjdk-17 aapt2 d8 apksigner rust cmake ninja clang make git

preflight.label: platform-jar
preflight.command: Place a user-provided Android SDK platform android.jar outside the repository and set ANDROID_JAR.

status.label: foreground
status.command: Confirm the simple smoke panel is visible; handle protected launch-check prompts manually.

cleanup.label: local-artifacts
cleanup.command: Leave build output under ignored local build directories; do not commit APKs, keystores, idsig files, jars, logs, or screenshots.

cleanup.label: transport
cleanup.command: Let the workflow that enabled WiFi ADB decide whether to keep it active or return to USB-only ADB.

evidence: Watchdog status showed an awake display and stay-awake state.
APK build produced a signed local artifact outside Git.
Install succeeded through the loopback ADB target.
Launch reached a visible public smoke panel after any operator-gated prompt was accepted.

risks.risk: WiFi ADB does not survive reboot, adbd restart, debugging timeout, or user revocation.
risks.recovery: Re-run the external authorization or pairing workflow and repeat the self-ADB gate.

risks.risk: A launch-check or controller prompt can look like an app launch failure.
risks.recovery: Use operator-visible headset input to satisfy the prompt, then classify it separately from build or install evidence.

risks.risk: Generated artifacts may contain signing material or device-specific details.
risks.recovery: Keep outputs in ignored build directories and run the public-boundary scanner before committing.

notes: This recipe proves the baseline APK loop, not full OpenXR rendering.
Use release assets or CI artifacts for binary APK distribution instead of committing APKs to Git history.
